questions.q: Who pays income tax on a sole proprietorship's profits?
choices: The owner, on their personal return
Nobody until the business is sold
The bank that finances the business
questions.explain: A proprietorship isn't a separate entity; the owner reports the profit personally.

questions.q: What liability does a general partner have?
choices: Only up to their capital contribution
Only for debts they personally signed
None, if the firm is registered
questions.explain: General partners are jointly liable for all debts incurred in the ordinary course of business.

questions.q: A junior partner signs a supply contract the agreement says only the senior partner may sign. Is the partnership bound?
choices: No, the agreement makes it void
Yes, every partner is an agent of the rest
Only if the supplier was told in writing
Only if all partners later ratify it
questions.explain: Each partner is an agent of the others; the partnership is bound, though partners can pursue the junior partner.

questions.q: What risk does a limited partner take by managing the business day to day?
choices: Losing their right to any profits
Being treated as a general partner
questions.explain: Taking part in management can cost a limited partner their limited liability.

questions.q: In an LLP, a partner is personally liable for whose negligence?
choices: Their own (or that they knew of)
questions.explain: LLP partners are liable for their own wrongs and ones they knew of and failed to prevent, not other partners'.

questions.q: Which professionals mainly use LLPs in BC?
questions.explain: LLPs are used mostly by law, notary and accounting firms.

questions.q: Which business form is a separate legal entity?
questions.explain: Only a corporation is a separate legal entity distinct from its owners.

questions.q: What do a corporation's shareholders own?
choices: A share of each of its assets
questions.explain: Shareholders own shares, not the company's assets.

questions.q: Why might a small-company shareholder still be personally liable for a loan?
choices: The lender required a personal guarantee
Corporate loans pass to the directors
questions.explain: Lenders to small corporations often demand personal guarantees, which bypass limited liability.

questions.q: What happens to a corporation when a shareholder dies?
choices: It carries on; shares pass on
Its assets go to the Crown
questions.explain: A corporation never dies; it carries on as shares change hands.

questions.q: Four partners each invest $25,000. A $250,000 judgment leaves a $150,000 shortfall. In a limited partnership with one general partner, who owes the $150,000?
questions.explain: Limited partners lose only their investment; the general partner has unlimited liability.

questions.q: How are a REIT's earnings generally taxed if CRA's rules are met?
choices: Twice: in the trust and in unitholders' hands
Not in the trust; unitholders pay
Only at the corporate tax rate
questions.explain: A qualifying REIT isn't taxed itself; unitholders pay tax on distributions.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · Other ways to invest together

questions.q: Which is a key advantage of REIT units?
choices: No market price risk at all
questions.explain: REITs combine limited liability, flow-through taxation and liquidity.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · Other ways to invest together

questions.q: What decides the liability and taxation of a joint venture?
questions.explain: A joint venture's liability and tax treatment depend on whether it's a partnership or corporation.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · Other ways to invest together

questions.q: Who holds trust assets for beneficiaries?
questions.explain: The trustee holds and manages assets for the beneficiaries.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · Other ways to invest together

questions.q: Does a PREC shield the licensee from liability for their real estate services?
choices: Yes, the corporation bears it all
Only if the PREC has E&O cover
questions.explain: The licensee remains personally liable for real estate services provided.

questions.q: Which is a benefit of earning commission through a PREC?
choices: No licence fees for the licensee
Tax deferral at a lower rate
questions.explain: A PREC can defer tax and benefit from a lower corporate rate.

questions.q: Which cost goes up with a PREC?
choices: Licence and E&O, as both need them
questions.explain: Both the licensee and the PREC must be licensed and carry E&O insurance.

questions.q: How must a PREC appear in advertising?
choices: As "PREC" right after the licensee name
By the licensee's first name only
questions.explain: The full words are required; the acronym "PREC" isn't permitted.

questions.q: Who can a PREC share income with through non-voting shares?
questions.explain: Limited income splitting is possible with a spouse or adult children through non-voting shares.

questions.q: Which standard must Canadian public companies use?
questions.explain: Since 2011, public companies must use International Financial Reporting Standards.

questions.q: Under ASPE, how is real estate usually shown?
questions.explain: ASPE keeps assets at historical cost less depreciation; IFRS allows fair value.

questions.q: Under the revenue recognition principle, when is a commission usually recognized?
choices: When the buyer first views it
When the cheque clears the bank
questions.explain: Revenue is recorded when earned, usually on transfer of title (or subject removal, depending on the contract).

questions.q: A year's insurance paid in January is spread over 12 months. Which principle is this?
questions.explain: Matching records expenses in the same periods as the revenue they help earn.

questions.q: Expensing a box of pens immediately instead of spreading it is allowed under which principle?
questions.explain: Materiality lets small items be expensed at once; it's an exception to matching.

questions.q: What is the longest a fiscal year can be?
questions.explain: A fiscal year can't exceed 53 weeks.

questions.q: Which accounting basis records rent when earned rather than when collected?
questions.explain: The accrual basis records revenue when earned and expenses when incurred.

questions.q: Is recoverable GST part of an asset's recorded cost?
choices: No, it is recovered as an ITC
questions.explain: GST that's recovered as an input tax credit isn't part of the asset's cost.

questions.q: Which equation is the basis of the balance sheet?
questions.explain: Assets equal liabilities plus owner's equity.

questions.q: A balance sheet shows a business's position:
questions.explain: The balance sheet is a snapshot at one point in time.

questions.q: Which is a current liability?
choices: Land held for the long term
questions.explain: Tenants' deposits are owed within the year; long-term mortgage debt is non-current.

questions.q: Which is a current asset?
questions.explain: Receivables convert to cash within the year.

questions.q: What does a balance sheet NOT show reliably?
choices: The amount of debt still owing
The market value of the business
The cash held in the bank account
questions.explain: Long-term assets appear at cost less depreciation, not market value.

questions.q: In a corporation, equity consists of:
questions.explain: Corporate equity is share capital plus retained earnings.

questions.q: What is net book value?
questions.explain: Net book value is historical cost less accumulated depreciation.

questions.q: Priya invests $150,000 and buys a $600,000 building with $120,000 down and a $480,000 mortgage. What are total assets?
questions.explain: $30,000 cash left + $600,000 property = $630,000, balanced by $480,000 debt + $150,000 equity.

questions.q: What is the "corporate veil"?
choices: Owners' names aren't on the statements
questions.explain: A corporation's statements show shares, not owners' names: the corporate veil.

questions.q: An income statement covers:
choices: Only the cash in the bank
questions.explain: The income statement shows revenue and expenses over a period.

questions.q: Which is NOT an expense on the income statement?
questions.explain: Principal reduces a liability; only interest is an expense.

questions.q: Which asset is never depreciated?
questions.explain: Land doesn't wear out and isn't depreciated.

questions.q: A building costs $350,000, salvage value $50,000, life 25 years. What's straight-line depreciation?
Opening inventory $50,000, purchases $200,000, closing inventory $60,000. Cost of goods sold?
Why does a proprietorship's income statement show no income tax?
choices: CRA collects it from the bank
questions.explain: The proprietor reports the business income on their personal return.

questions.q: Which is a non-cash expense?
questions.explain: Depreciation reduces income without any cash leaving the business.

questions.q: Net income links the income statement to which balance sheet item?
questions.explain: Net income increases owner's equity (retained earnings in a corporation).

questions.q: Assets worth $650,000 at market, debts $250,000, price $520,000. What's goodwill?
Goodwill is the amount paid above:
choices: The assessed value of the land
The market value of net assets
The book value of the building
questions.explain: Goodwill = price − market value of net assets.

questions.q: For tax purposes, CRA allows:
questions.explain: CRA requires capital cost allowance at prescribed rates, not accounting depreciation.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · The tax return and capital cost allowance

questions.q: What's the CCA rate for many Class 1 buildings?
questions.explain: Class 1 buildings are 4% on a declining balance.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · The tax return and capital cost allowance

questions.q: What does the half-year rule do?
choices: Doubles the CCA in the year of sale
Halves the rate in the year acquired
Halves the capital gain on a sale
questions.explain: In the year of acquisition, only 50% of the normal rate can be claimed.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · The tax return and capital cost allowance

questions.q: How much CCA can be claimed in the year an asset is sold?
questions.explain: No CCA is allowed in the year of disposal.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · The tax return and capital cost allowance

questions.q: An owner skips CCA one year. Can they claim double next year?
questions.explain: CCA is optional, but unused amounts can't be doubled up later.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · The tax return and capital cost allowance

questions.q: What is recapture?
choices: A lender's right to seize property
CCA added back to income on sale
A refund of overpaid property tax
questions.explain: If an asset sells above its UCC, excess CCA claimed is added back to taxable income.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · The tax return and capital cost allowance

questions.q: Year-one CCA on a $350,000 Class 1 building (4%, half-year rule)?
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · The tax return and capital cost allowance

questions.q: Why is CCA called a tax shelter?
choices: It defers tax without spending cash
It exempts rent from income tax
It removes GST from the sale
questions.explain: CCA is a non-cash deduction that defers tax, paid later in cheaper dollars.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · The tax return and capital cost allowance

questions.q: Which businesses file their own business tax return?
questions.explain: Proprietors and partners report on personal returns; corporations file their own.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · The tax return and capital cost allowance

questions.q: Do you need a real estate licence to sell a business that owns no real estate?
questions.explain: No real estate means no trade in real estate.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · Selling a business: do you need a licence?

questions.q: A business sale includes the assignment of its lease. Is a licence needed?
choices: No, a lease isn't real estate
Yes, a lease is an interest in land
Only if the lease is over 3 years
questions.explain: Assigning a lease is a trade in real estate.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · Selling a business: do you need a licence?

questions.q: Selling 60% of the shares of a company that owns a warehouse is:
questions.explain: Less than 100% of shares is a securities trade, possibly under the Securities Act.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · Selling a business: do you need a licence?

questions.q: Selling 100% of the shares of a company that owns real estate:
questions.explain: Selling all the shares of a real-estate-holding company is a trade in real estate.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · Selling a business: do you need a licence?

questions.q: The income statement given to a business buyer should cover 12 months ending no more than how many days before signing?
questions.explain: 12 months ending not more than 120 days before the agreement is signed.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · Selling a business: do you need a licence?

questions.q: Which document should a business buyer get along with the statements?
questions.explain: Buyers need the income statement, balance sheet and a list of excluded fixtures, chattels and assets.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · Selling a business: do you need a licence?

questions.q: Who can do conveyancing for a fee in BC?
questions.explain: Only lawyers and notaries can convey for a fee.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · After the subjects come off

questions.q: Who usually chooses the conveyancer?
questions.explain: The buyer usually pays for the conveyance, so the buyer chooses.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · After the subjects come off

questions.q: Which document transfers title in BC?
questions.explain: The Form A Freehold Transfer transfers title.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · After the subjects come off

questions.q: When does the buyer's conveyancer pay out the sale funds?
choices: On the day of subject removal
questions.explain: Payment is made once the documents appear as pending applications on title.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · After the subjects come off

questions.q: Which document is needed for a strata lot sale?
questions.explain: A Form F shows strata fees are paid.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · After the subjects come off

questions.q: Which is NOT an automatic exception in the standard title clause?
questions.explain: Private easements and covenants must be added to the clause.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · Your contract has to be right

questions.q: In JBP Developments v. Li, what happened to the deposit?
choices: It was forfeited to the seller
It was returned to the buyer
questions.explain: An unlisted restrictive covenant meant the seller couldn't give the promised title; the buyer got the deposit back.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · Your contract has to be right

questions.q: Title terms in a contract are:
questions.explain: Title terms are essential conditions; breach lets the buyer terminate.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · Your contract has to be right

questions.q: What can a licensee lose if a title error lets the buyer walk away?
questions.explain: With no enforceable contract, commission may not be earned, and the licensee may be liable.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · Your contract has to be right

questions.q: When are taxes and rent switched to the buyer?
questions.explain: The adjustment date allocates costs and income between the parties.

questions.q: What's the safest possession timing?
questions.explain: Closing can take hours; possession the day after completion avoids problems.

questions.q: A licensee handed buyers keys a day early and they set off an alarm. Result?
choices: No penalty, as no harm was done
questions.explain: The licensee was reprimanded and ordered to pay $1,500 for failing to use reasonable care.

questions.q: The adjustment date is usually the same as:
questions.explain: Adjustment usually matches possession.

questions.q: How can title insurance help when a survey reveals an encroachment?
questions.explain: Title insurance can let a lender advance funds despite an encroachment, or replace a survey.

questions.q: Which two types of title insurance policy are there?
questions.explain: Owner's policies (for buyers) and lender's policies.

questions.q: Why does the seller hand over the signed transfer before being paid?
choices: They rely on the lawyer's undertaking
The law requires it of all sellers
questions.explain: A conveyancer's undertaking is a binding professional promise to pay.

questions.q: Which closing cost can't be added to the mortgage?
questions.explain: PST on mortgage default insurance must be paid in cash at closing.

questions.q: An interest adjustment covers interest from:
choices: The listing date to the sale date
questions.explain: It covers interest from the advance date to the start of the first regular payment period.

questions.q: What does the buyer's statement of adjustments show as its bottom line?
questions.explain: The buyer's statement shows the balance due to complete.

questions.q: On a statement of adjustments, a credit to a party means:
choices: They paid it or are owed it
questions.explain: A credit is already paid by, or owed to, that party.

questions.q: If an item appears on both statements, it appears:
choices: On the same side of both
questions.explain: An item on both statements is a debit on one and a credit on the other.

questions.q: Are the buyer's and seller's statements mirror images?
choices: No, items can be on one only
Only in sales of strata lots
Only when there is a VTB
questions.explain: Items like the deposit, commission and PTT appear on only one statement.

questions.q: Where does a deposit held by the brokerage appear?
questions.explain: The deposit is a credit to the buyer and doesn't appear on the seller's statement.

questions.q: Where does the commission appear?
questions.explain: Commission is the seller's debt; it's a debit on the seller's statement only.

questions.q: A new first mortgage from a bank appears:
choices: Debit to buyer and credit to seller
As a credit to the buyer only
As a debit to the seller only
questions.explain: New third-party financing is a credit on the buyer's statement only.

questions.q: A vendor take-back mortgage appears:
choices: As a credit to the buyer only
As a debit to the seller only
questions.explain: The seller takes back part of the price as a mortgage: credit buyer, debit seller.

questions.q: The seller's mortgage being paid off appears:
choices: As a credit to the buyer only
As a debit to the seller only
questions.explain: The payout is a debit on the seller's statement only.

questions.q: Property transfer tax appears:
choices: As a debit to the seller
As a debit to the buyer only
questions.explain: PTT is the buyer's cost: a debit on the buyer's statement only.

questions.q: Tenants' security deposits plus interest appear as:
questions.explain: The new owner must repay them, so they're credited to the buyer and debited to the seller.

questions.q: In what capacity does the brokerage hold the deposit?
choices: As a trustee for the city
questions.explain: The brokerage holds the deposit as stakeholder until completion.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · The deposit and the commission are separate

questions.q: The deposit is $45,000 and commission $31,500. Where does the extra $13,500 go?
questions.explain: The brokerage keeps the commission and sends the excess to the conveyancer.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · The deposit and the commission are separate

questions.q: The buyer is responsible for property taxes from:
choices: The day after the adjustment date
The completion date of the sale
questions.explain: The buyer pays from and including the adjustment date.

questions.q: Seller prepaid annual taxes of $3,650. Adjustment date September 1. What's the adjustment?
When the seller has prepaid the taxes, the adjustment is:
questions.explain: The buyer repays the seller for the buyer's share.

questions.q: Taxes for the year ($3,650) aren't yet paid. Adjustment date March 1 (non-leap year). Seller's share?
When taxes are due but unpaid, who bears the late penalty?
questions.explain: The full tax and penalty are charged to the seller; the penalty isn't adjusted.

questions.q: If either party isn't eligible for the home owner grant, taxes are adjusted on:
questions.explain: Gross taxes are used unless both parties qualify for the basic grant.

questions.q: Rent of $2,400 was collected for September. Adjustment date September 21. Buyer's credit?
Rent collected in advance by the seller produces:
questions.explain: The buyer is owed rent from the adjustment date to month-end.

questions.q: Debits on the buyer's statement total $918,420 and credits $765,000. Balance due to complete?
What is PTT on a $900,000 home (1% on first $200,000, 2% above)?
In the case discussed, how liable was the listing licensee for missing a fraud visible in the statements?
questions.explain: The listing licensee was held 15% liable.

questions.q: How is heating oil left in the tank usually settled?
choices: As a debit to the buyer
As a credit to the seller
questions.explain: Items like furnace oil are usually settled outside the statements.

questions.q: What does the marketing concept put first?
questions.explain: The marketing concept starts with client needs.

questions.q: What long-term business mix should a licensee aim for?
questions.explain: About two-thirds repeat and referral, one-third new.

questions.q: Which marketing strategy best suits an individual licensee?
questions.explain: Niche marketing focuses resources on one small, growing segment.

questions.q: A residential licensee is offered a complex commercial listing. Best response?
choices: Take it and learn as you go
List it at a lower price
questions.explain: Taking work beyond your competence risks your duty of competence; refer it for a fee.

questions.q: A positioning map plots competitors on:
questions.explain: Positioning maps compare competitors on two attributes to find gaps.

questions.q: Which three needs does a licensee satisfy?
questions.explain: Information; knowledge and skills; trust and confidentiality.

questions.q: Real estate services are which kind of good?
questions.explain: Consumers compare options before buying: shopping goods.

questions.q: Life insurance and fire extinguishers are examples of:
questions.explain: Unsought goods aren't sought until prompted.

questions.q: How many licensees does a seller typically interview?
questions.explain: Sellers typically interview around three licensees.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · The process model of buying

questions.q: Most clients decide on a licensee within how long of finishing their research?
questions.explain: Most decide within a week, so stay in touch.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · The process model of buying

questions.q: Doubt and regret after a purchase is called:
questions.explain: Post-purchase cognitive dissonance, or buyer's remorse.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · The process model of buying

questions.q: In commercial real estate, what matters more to clients than in residential?
questions.explain: Commercial clients put more weight on the brokerage's reputation.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · The process model of buying

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the 4 Ps?
questions.explain: The 4 Ps are product, place, price and promotion.

questions.q: Which promotional element is least controllable?
questions.explain: Publicity is unpaid media coverage you can't control.

questions.q: Pricing low to win market share is called:
questions.explain: Penetration pricing sets a low price to gain share.

questions.q: Coaching a kids' team or joining a service club is:
questions.explain: Community involvement builds goodwill: public relations.

questions.q: What does the "M" in SMART stand for?
questions.explain: Specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, timely.

questions.q: Why is percentage-of-sales budgeting called backwards?
questions.explain: Spending follows sales, so it falls when sales fall, just when ads are needed.

questions.q: Which budget method is considered most logical?
questions.explain: Set objectives, then cost the tasks needed to reach them.

questions.q: What does AIDA stand for?
questions.explain: The classic message sequence: attention, interest, desire, action.

questions.q: Which sources are seen as more credible?
questions.explain: Friends, family and word of mouth are more credible than formal ads.

questions.q: Where does a reader's eye usually land first on an ad?
questions.explain: Eyes land near the 10 o'clock position, so put the headline there.

questions.q: What should ad copy end with?
questions.explain: Good copy ends by telling the reader what to do next.

questions.q: Who may NOT do telemarketing for a licensee?
questions.explain: Unlicensed assistants can't telemarket.

questions.q: Google Ads appear as:
questions.explain: Google Ads are paid placements, separate from organic results.

questions.q: Which Rules section deals with personal offices?
questions.explain: Section 37 bars signs, phone answering in the brokerage's name and personal office addresses in ads.

questions.q: Under s.40, the brokerage's name in an ad must be:
questions.explain: The licensed brokerage name must be prominent and easily readable; a logo isn't enough.

questions.q: Advertising a property for sale without the owner's consent breaches:
questions.explain: Section 42 requires the owner's (or their agent's) consent.

questions.q: Which team name is acceptable?
questions.explain: "Real Estate" is allowed only as "Real Estate Team/Group" at the end.

questions.q: In April 2025, BCFSA fines for unqualified "#1" claims ranged from:
questions.explain: Four licensees were fined $4,000 to $6,250.

questions.q: Which Competition Act section bans charging more than the advertised price?
questions.explain: Section 74.05 covers sale above the advertised price.

questions.q: Which is a common advertising violation BCFSA sees?
choices: Ads in more than one language
Ads that list too many photos
questions.explain: Missing or tiny brokerage names, unregistered teams and personal office signage are most common.

questions.q: Why include expired listings in a CMA?
choices: To show that the market is slowing
To reveal pricing or marketing errors
To fill out the extra pages
questions.explain: Expired listings can show properties that were overpriced or poorly marketed.

questions.q: How should you deliver the in-person presentation?
choices: Speak only to the main owner
questions.explain: Make it a dialogue, avoid jargon and present to all the sellers.

questions.q: Any statistics you claim in a listing presentation must be:
questions.explain: Claims must be accurate and verifiable.

questions.q: How should you find the listing's key message?
choices: Copy the last ad you ran
questions.explain: Ask what made the sellers fall in love with the property.

questions.q: Who is responsible for the accuracy of MLS® listing data?
questions.explain: The listing licensee is responsible for the data's accuracy.

questions.q: Which photo edit is acceptable?
questions.explain: Removing temporary items is fine; altering physical features misleads.

questions.q: Drones from 250 g to 25 kg require:
questions.explain: Transport Canada requires a pilot certificate and drone registration.

questions.q: SEO aims to improve your ranking in:
questions.explain: SEO targets unpaid, organic results.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · Websites, SEO and social media

questions.q: How often should newsletters go out?
questions.explain: No more than weekly and at least quarterly.
questions.ref: Lesson 16 · Websites, SEO and social media

questions.q: Where must the brokerage name appear on social media?
questions.explain: On the profile; it needn't be in every post.

questions.q: Where does the brokerage name go on YouTube?
questions.explain: Put it in the title or description (or the video intro).

questions.q: Can you translate your brokerage's name for a Punjabi-language post?
questions.explain: Brokerage names must not be translated.

questions.q: On Craigslist and Kijiji, the brokerage name must appear:
questions.explain: Each posting needs the brokerage name.

questions.q: CASL applies to:
questions.explain: CASL covers CEMs: emails, texts and similar messages.

questions.q: Which is NOT valid express consent under CASL?
questions.explain: Pre-checked boxes don't count as express consent.

questions.q: Implied consent from a business relationship lasts:
questions.explain: Implied consent from a relationship lasts two years.

questions.q: Maximum CASL penalty for a business?
questions.explain: Up to $1 million for individuals and $10 million for businesses.

questions.q: Every CEM must include:
questions.explain: Identification, contact details and a free unsubscribe.

questions.q: The Electronic Transactions Act does NOT cover:
questions.explain: Registrable documents that create or transfer an interest in land are excluded.

questions.q: Is a sender's name at the bottom of an email a valid signature?
questions.explain: BCFSA says a name in an email isn't enough.

questions.q: What should be kept with a DocuSigned contract?
choices: A paper copy of each email
questions.explain: The Certificate of Completion proves who signed and when.

questions.q: How long must brokerage records be kept?
questions.explain: Rules s.92 requires 7 years.

questions.q: Where must brokerage records be kept under RESA s.25?
questions.explain: Records must be kept in BC.

questions.q: Copyright protects:
questions.explain: Copyright protects the expression, not the underlying facts.

questions.q: Minimum recommended password length?
questions.explain: At least 8 characters with mixed types.

questions.q: What's the first line of defence against attacks?
questions.explain: Your router's firewall is the first line of defence.

questions.q: Backups should be kept in how many physical locations?
questions.explain: Keep backups in two physical locations.

questions.q: Which is one of BCFSA's AI tips?
questions.explain: You're responsible for anything AI produces, so fact-check it.

questions.q: Which is NOT personal information under PIPA?
questions.explain: Business contact information is excluded.

questions.q: When must you state your purpose for collecting personal information?
questions.explain: Purpose must be disclosed on or before collection.

questions.q: What should you do with personal information no longer needed?
questions.explain: Destroy it or make it anonymous.

questions.q: Before posting listing details online you need:
questions.explain: Get the seller's written consent.
